info.name: Orvexa API v1
info.description:
Orvexa — the AI-native Contact Center OS. Full v1 surface (api/openapi/orvexa-v1.yaml) organized by domain and ordered as the end-to-end integration journey:

health → customer → resolution → agents & presence → conversation → interaction lifecycle → routing decision → AI suggestion & governed tools → outbound call → messages → case & notes → durable workflow → analytics → search → identity → signed provider webhook.

## Setup

Set the collection variables before running:

- `ORVEXA_URL` — API base URL (e.g. `http://localhost:8080`)
- `ORVEXA_KEY` — tenant API key (`X-API-Key`). Never commit a real key.
- `ORVEXA_SECRET` — webhook HMAC secret (`ORVEXA_WEBHOOK_HMAC_SECRET` on the server). Never commit it.

Requests capture resource ids into collection variables (`customer_id`, `interaction_id`, `call_id`, …) so the whole journey runs top-to-bottom with *Run Collection*. Every request carries a `pm.test` status snippet.

## Envelope

Success responses use `{data, meta}`; errors use `{error:{code, message, details?}}`.

## Signed webhooks

`POST /api/v1/webhooks/{provider}` is public but HMAC-verified: `X-Orvexa-Signature: hex(HMAC-SHA256(ORVEXA_SECRET, rawBody))` (see the Webhooks folder — the pre-request script computes both the body and its signature). Provider-registered verifiers (twilio, whatsappcloud, africastalking) use their carrier schemes instead — see docs/runbooks/operations.md § Webhook signatures.

Import instructions: docs/api-clients.md. Ground truth: api/openapi/orvexa-v1.yaml.

exec: // The tenant always derives from the API key — never from a request body.

item.name: Health & Discovery
item.description: Liveness and component-truth probes (journey gate: `/readyz` must report `ready` before any business call). Public — no API key — plus the authenticated `GET /api/v1/` resource index (surface map).

request.description: Component truth. 200 `ready` when the DB is up; 503 `degraded` names the down component truthfully.
Process liveness — always 200 while the API is serving.
Authenticated resource index — the machine-readable surface map ({data.resources[]}). Requires the API key (401 auth.missing_key without it).

item.name: Customers
item.description: Customer identity: create with channel identifiers, resolve an identifier back to a customer, paginate.

request.description: Identifiers are normalized (phone → E.164 digits, email lowercase). (tenant, type, value) is unique — an identifier can never fork into two customers.
Normalization means `254712345678`, `+254712345678` and `+254 712 345 678` resolve to the same customer.

item.name: Conversations
item.description: Customer-facing threads. Inbound interactions without a conversation_id find-or-open the customer's open conversation for the channel.

exec: pm.test("first pass: conversations open in the Interactions folder — run the tour again", () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

request.description: Interaction records of this conversation. NOTE: the current build serializes interaction records with Go field names (e.g. `ID`, `Status`) — see docs/api-clients.md “Live wire contract notes”.

exec: pm.test("first pass: conversations open in the Interactions folder — run the tour again", () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

request.description: Needs the ids captured in the Agents/Queues folders (later in the tour) — green on a second pass or when running folders in journey order.

exec: pm.test("waiting for Agents/Queues ids (later in the tour) — run the tour again", () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

request.description: Terminal state — a closed conversation is sealed. Run deliberately at the end of the journey.

exec: pm.test("first pass: conversations open in the Interactions folder — run the tour again", () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

item.name: Interactions
item.description:
The unified interaction abstraction across voice/whatsapp/sms/email/chat/ussd. Lifecycle: pending → active → wrapup → completed|failed|canceled (guarded; illegal moves answer 409 with the allowed set).

Wire contract: request and response keys are the snake_case names of api/openapi/orvexa-v1.yaml (issue #101 fix) — e.g. the create body sends `customer_id` and records serialize as `id`/`status`/….

request.description: Inbound + no conversationid → find-or-open the customer's open conversation for the channel. Externally-triggered creates should carry `idempotencykey` (pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{8,128}$) so replays are single-effect.
to ∈ pending|active|wrapup|completed|failed|canceled. Illegal moves → 409 with error.details.allowed.

item.name: Agents
item.description: Human agent registry, skills and presence (available|busy|wrapup|offline).

item.name: Queues
item.description: Routing queues with priority, SLA and required skills.

item.name: Cases
item.description: Case lifecycle: open → in_progress → pending_customer → resolved → closed (+ reopen from resolved; canceled). Serialized per-tenant reference, notes, interaction links.

request.description: author_type ∈ agent|ai_agent|system; body ≤ 8000 chars.
204 No Content on success. Links the chat interaction captured in the Interactions folder — swap `{{interaction_id}}` for `{{call_id}}` to link the voice call instead.
to ∈ open|in_progress|pending_customer|resolved|closed|canceled; closed is terminal; reopen is legal from resolved.

item.name: Calls
item.description: Outbound telephony. PlaceCall creates a pending voice interaction and hands the leg to the provider (simulator by default); lifecycle progress arrives as signed provider webhooks.

request.description: Returns immediately (201) — ringing/connected/ended arrive via signed webhooks. The simulator delivers the full loop locally.
action ∈ answer|hangup|transfer|hold|resume|complete. transfer needs `destination`.

item.name: Messages
item.description: Outbound messaging (whatsapp|sms|email) — creates the outbound interaction and hands delivery to the provider.

body.raw:
{
  "customer_id": "{{customer_id}}",
  "channel": "sms",
  "from": "orvexa-sms",
  "to": "+254712345678",
  "body": "Your ticket is resolved. Reply STOP to opt out."
}

request.description: `from` is optional in api/openapi/orvexa-v1.yaml but required by this build (endpoints check) — include it. body ≤ 4096 chars; media_urls for MMS-style sends.

item.name: Routing
item.description: Deterministic routing engine: score candidates (skills coverage, presence, priority), record immutable decisions.

request.description: Returns the decision (agent/queue/fallback outcome). Decisions are deterministic — same inputs, same answer.

item.name: AI
item.description: Governed AI: one metered turn per invoke (advisory suggestions only), tool execution through the allowlist gateway (schema + rate + audit).

request.description: Runtime view of the agent configuration (model hint, tool limits, policies).
Metered: token usage is counted and clamped to the configured cap. Suggestions are advisory — never auto-executed.

⚠ Live wire contract note: the tool-call body binds to Go field names in this build (`Tool`/`InteractionID`/`Args`; `tool`/`args` also match case-insensitively, but snake_case `interaction_id` does not) — diverging from the OpenAPI enum block. Allowlist: get_customer | create_case | send_whatsapp. 403 when not allowed, 429 when rate-capped; refusals are audited.

item.name: Workflows
item.description: Durable workflow executions (callback ladder, collections ladder). Instances are resumable and cancelable.

request.description: schedule_at optional (RFC3339) — omitted means start immediately/at the first rung.
409 when the instance is not cancelable (already terminal).

item.name: Analytics
item.description: Facts aggregation (PostgreSQL by default, ClickHouse when configured).

item.name: Search
item.description: Full-text conversation search over the OpenSearch read model. Degradation principle: a search outage never blocks the hot path.

query.description: Simple query string over projected search text, customer and channel (1–256 chars)

request.description: 200 hits (eventually consistent) — or the typed degradation: 503 `search.not_configured` (backend unset) / `search.unavailable` (backend down). Tenant scope is enforced server-side from the API key.

exec: pm.test("status is 200 or typed 503 degradation", () => pm.expect([200, 503]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: Identity
item.description: OIDC login surface ([O-29]). Mounted ONLY when ORVEXA_OIDC_* is configured; otherwise the routes answer 404 `identity.disabled`. Public — no API key.

request.description: 200 {authorize_url, state, nonce, expires_in, redirect_uri} when the identity plane is configured. NOTE: on a deployment without OIDC the route is not mounted and the raw 404 body is the router's plain-text `404 page not found` (not the JSON error envelope).

exec: pm.test("status is 200 or 404 (identity plane disabled)", () => pm.expect([200, 404]).to.include(pm.response.code));

query.description: Authorization code from the IdP redirect

request.description: State validation → code exchange → ID-token verification → tenant-scoped principal info. Drive this through a real IdP redirect; direct calls answer 401/404.

item.name: Webhooks
item.description:
Public provider ingress: POST /api/v1/webhooks/{provider}. Signature required (fail-closed), single-effect dedup on the raw body, IP-rate-limited. The pre-request script computes BOTH the payload and its platform signature — exactly what scripts/e2e-demo.sh does with openssl:

    SIG=$(printf '%s' "$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$ORVEXA_SECRET" -hex | awk '{print $2}')

Providers with a registered verifier (twilio, whatsappcloud, africastalking) are validated by their carrier scheme instead — see docs/runbooks/operations.md § Webhook signatures.

Journey note: run the Interactions folder first — the signed event references an existing `interaction_id` (the provider contract drives an existing interaction's lifecycle).

request.description: The pre-request script builds `{event, interaction_id, tenant_id, detail}` and signs the EXACT raw bytes: `X-Orvexa-Signature = hex(HMAC-SHA256(ORVEXA_SECRET, body))`. A one-byte body change rejects. 202 accepted on first delivery.

exec: // Build the provider payload against the CURRENT interaction, then
// sign the exact raw bytes with the shared HMAC secret

request.description: The idempotency key is derived from the raw body: the replay returns the ORIGINAL event id with `duplicate: true` (HTTP 200) and applies no second effect.
Negative test: no signature header → 401 `webhook.invalid_signature`, nothing persisted. The gateway never opens an unsigned ingestion path.
